standard_prerequisites.name: A finitely presented module over a localization is the localization of a finite module over the base
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite R-module M whose localization is L.

standard_prerequisites.name: A regular local ring has finite global dimension, so every finite module has a finite free resolution
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns M into a perfect complex, hence into a class in K_0(R_f).

standard_prerequisites.name: The K-group computation for perfect complexes and the determinant map on K_0
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the class of L is a multiple of the class of R_f, and the determinant then forces triviality.

core_obligations: Let L be an invertible R_f-module, so in particular a finite R_f-module, and use the Algebra statement on constructing finitely presented modules to find a finite R-module M with M_f isomorphic to L (proof lines 36786-36789).
Use the Algebra proposition on finite global dimension of a regular local ring to obtain a finite free resolution F_bullet of M over R (proof lines 36790-36791).
Conclude that L is quasi-isomorphic to a finite complex of free R_f-modules (proof lines 36792-36793).
Use the statement relating perfect complexes to the K-group to conclude that [L_f] = n[R_f] in K_0(R_f) for some integer n (proof lines 36793-36795).
Apply the determinant map to conclude that L is trivial (proof lines 36796-36797).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a regular local ring R and an element f, and asserts that Pic(R_f) = 0 (source lines 36779-36783). The proof is a K-theoretic argument. Let L be an invertible R_f-module; in particular L is a finite R_f-module, so there is a finite R-module M with M_f isomorphic to L, quoting the Algebra statement on constructing finitely presented modules realizing a given localization (proof lines 36786-36789). By the Algebra proposition on the finite global dimension of a regular local ring, M has a finite free resolution F_bullet over R (proof lines 36790-36791). It follows that L is quasi-isomorphic to a finite complex of free R_f-modules (proof lines 36792-36793). Hence by the statement relating perfect complexes to the K-group, [L_f] = n[R_f] in K_0(R_f) for some integer n (proof lines 36793-36795). Applying the determinant map then shows that L is trivial, which is the conclusion (proof lines 36796-36797). The non-routine content is the route: a line bundle on R_f is realized by a finite module over R, finite global dimension of the regular local ring gives a finite free resolution, and the resulting vanishing in the reduced K_0 together with the determinant map forces triviality. Note that the author leaves the final determinant step to be read off from the cited map.
